changes: xiongnu: keyframe_review xiongnu_-110, _-91, _-66, _-50, _-40, _6, _14, _30, _51, _60, _68, _78, _84: correction now a minus of the old shape and the Hexi Corridor (all), the Ordos (-91..30), the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (-50, -40, 6, 14) and a 100 km disc round Turpan (-66); 'ok' keyframes became 'adjust'
xiongnu: ledger (67 BCE loss to han-dynasty): region narrowed from Turfan-Hami to a 100 km disc round Turpan
han-dynasty: ledger/35 (67 BCE gain from xiongnu): same narrowing, mirror of the xiongnu loss
lu-fang: ledger/1 (42 loss): counterpart xiongnu -> nobody (ends the 43-51 Inner Mongolia conflict)
findings.why: The Gansu, Ordos and Turfan cells that the size rule gave the Xiongnu came from Cliopatria Xiongnu shapes that still cover land the Han held (Hexi from 121 BCE, Ordos from 127 BCE, Turfan from 67 BCE, the Tarim from 60 BCE); the keyframes now leave it out. Not fixed: Xinjiang 74 and 91 (about 2,400 and 2,200 cells): the Tarim stays with the Xiongnu after its vassal_end of 74 because han-dynasty's vassal_start of the protectorate is applied earlier in the same year (month 0, dossier order) than the xiongnu vassal_end, so the relation closes empty; a dossier cannot change that without inventing a month. -127, -126, -111 (Han wins) are right as they are.

changes: han-dynasty: keyframe_review han-dynasty_184: from 184, to 186 (it had no 'to' and ran to 196)
han-dynasty: keyframes han-dynasty_188, _190, _191, _193, _194: minus Liang Province (Gansu, Ningxia), as _187 and _195 already do
han-dynasty: ledger/98 (196 loss): counterpart han-sui -> nobody
findings.why: The 187-196 claims came mainly from the 184 keyframe keeping the whole nominal realm alive to 196, and from five keyframes that put Liang Province back after the 187 loss to the Liang rebels (Han Sui page: 'Han Sui and Ma Teng declared themselves co-rulers of Liang Province'; retreat 'back to Liang Province' in 192). Ledger/98 gave han-sui Shaanxi, Qinghai and Ordos cells that han-sui.json no longer draws; the page has no Yong, Guanzhong or submission in 196-200. The vassal pair 197-211 is not added: data/hierarchy.csv supplies it. Ledger/103 (211 gain from han-sui) left: the Han/Cao Cao duplication is the open point named in the han-dynasty notes. The Baoji circle (han-sui found 189, Han until 196) is not on the page and is left as it is.

The 196 snap restored the 184 realm (17,063 cells = the 184 shape plus Hami) because keyframe 184 had no 'to'; the 197 keyframe (1,191 cells) then removed 7,341 of them. The ledger 84-100 already ends on exactly the 1,191 cells of keyframe 196 (checked with the gazetteer). Mechanical fix, no date or place changed, so no new page.

changes: han-dynasty: keyframes han-dynasty_25, _27, _29, _30, _34, _36, _37, _40: minus Lu Fang's Inner Mongolia (Ordos and Hetao)
lu-fang: ledger/1 (42 loss): counterpart xiongnu -> nobody
findings.why: Guangwu page: 'He, supported by Xiongnu's Chanyu Yu, controlled the modern central and western Inner Mongolia region'; 'eventually fled to Xiongnu in AD 42'; nothing on who held the land afterwards. The size rule already gave Lu Fang the land in 24-40, but the Han keyframes re-claimed it every time, so they now cut it (the option the classifier named). No Han loss event added: the page gives no year for the rise and the event would be a no-op after Lu Fang's found.

findings.why: The Donghu gain only moves the cells the donghu dossier holds (north Hebei, south-east Inner Mongolia, west Liaoning), so 5,089 cells had to be snapped on. Modu Chanyu page: 'By 208 BCE, the Donghu had been defeated'; 'The eastern border stretched as far as the Liao River'. Checked with the gazetteer: homeland event plus the new gain equal the corrected keyframe exactly (14,678 cells).

Same cause as F036: keyframe 184 ('holds 184-186' in its own note) had no 'to' and ran to 196, so the 196 union of live keyframes was 17,063 cells while the ledger had 5,436 after the losses to the warlords. Mechanical.
